posts.title: Retro #19: November (part 1)
posts.description: This month I’ve had a lot of things on the brain, so we’re doing a mid-month retro… a midterm, if you will. (I’d like to extend some congrats to our friends south of the border on those; absolutely fantastic work. Among many other things, I loved these photos .) To be honest, I’d love to do weekly retros like Jenn does, but I’m chicken! Commitments are immediate stressors to me… and what if I promise I’ll do them every week and then don’t … there’s a lot to unpack there, I guess. posts.title: Retro #18: October
posts.description: This retro is the first post that I’m also sending to my email list! If you’re reading this on the blog or RSS and would like to get email notifications, here’s the link ! In October I finally got around to writing my eulogy for the 2026 Blue Jays , and I’m really happy with how it turned out. It got a lot of really nice feedback and a friend told me they loved it even though they don’t care about sports, which is the highest possible praise, IMO. Last year when I wrote about the 2025 team I also wrote about how hard that was to write, particularly because I was so out of practice; this one was a little easier, or at least less of a struggle, which I will consider a victory. When I re-read it I still find all kinds of things I should have spent more time on (why do the tenses disagree there, is this idea really tied in the way I wanted to, etc) but overall I’m proud of it and I appreciate all the comments! posts.title: 2026: It wasn’t supposed to end like this
posts.description: On September 27th, 42-year-old presumptive Hall of Famer Max Scherzer walked out to the mound in a Blue Jays uniform to, improbably, pitch the eighth inning. He wasn’t coming out in relief; he’d been pitching the entire afternoon, starting on three days’ rest in what might turn out to be the final game of his career. He hadn’t seen the eighth inning since August 2025, when he pitched to one batter in the eighth before being relieved, and before that, not since August 2023. None of this was exactly routine. It wasn’t supposed to end this way for him, not if you’d been paying attention all year; he’d been ineffective, with a bloated ERA and a tendency toward unraveling in the first inning before getting it together for a few more. There were injuries, brutally short starts, hard contact.
